name: The Spirit in Creation, Revelation, and Inspiration
path: Pneumatology: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit

objectives.text: Identify from Genesis 1:2 that the Spirit of God was present and at work when God made the world
Recall that the Holy Spirit moved the prophets and apostles to speak and write God's words in the Bible
Retell from Job and the Psalms how the Spirit gives breath and life to people and creatures
Recite Psalm 119:18 as a class prayer asking God for understanding before reading Scripture together
Explain in simple words what it means that all Scripture is breathed out by God
Identify Old Testament passages that show the Spirit speaking through prophets and leaders
Describe how the Spirit continues to sustain and renew creation as part of God's providence
Explain how the Spirit filled Bezalel with skill for crafting the tabernacle and what this shows about the Spirit's work in human abilities
Explain how Jesus' promise that the Spirit would remind the apostles of his words and guide them into truth relates to the writing of the New Testament
Distinguish general revelation from special revelation and describe the Spirit's role in giving special revelation
Compare inspiration, the Spirit's giving of the Word, with illumination, the Spirit's enabling of readers to understand it
Analyze how New Testament writers introduce Old Testament quotations as the speech of the Holy Spirit
Interpret 2 Peter 1:20-21 in its context to explain how human authors were carried along by the Spirit while their own personalities and styles remained
Explain how the Reformed tradition grounds the authority, infallibility, and inerrancy of Scripture in the Spirit's inspiration
Explain the inward testimony of the Spirit as the Westminster Confession describes it and distinguish it from the external evidences for Scripture
Compare verbal plenary inspiration with dictation and partial inspiration views and explain why the Reformed tradition holds the first
Construct a written account of the Spirit's work in creation, providence, and revelation that shows how it fits within the shared work of the Father, Son, and Spirit
Evaluate the Reformed claim that the Holy Spirit speaking in Scripture is the supreme judge over church councils, traditions, and private claims to revelation
Defend the Holy Spirit as the ultimate Author of Scripture against common objections such as human authorship and alleged errors
Evaluate the Reformed teaching that the Spirit's testimony, rather than church authority or rational proofs alone, is the final ground of certainty that Scripture is God's Word

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Spirit in creation, Spirit moving the prophets, inspiration, inspiration versus illumination, 2 Peter 1:21, authority and inerrancy, inward testimony, the theology of creation and revelation, the Spirit as Author, the ground of certainty). I dropped 'Explain how the Spirit guides believers into truth' as a general claim about believers and refocused it on Jesus' promise to the apostles. I turned 'Apply dependence on the Spirit' into a classroom prayer practice based on Psalm 119:18. I recast 'Analyze the Spirit's inward witness' and the grade 9 internal testimony item as one explanation tied to WCF 1.5, and moved the certainty synthesis into an evaluation. I reframed the new revelation claim around WCF 1.10 as the supreme judge so it does not overlap the gifts and cessationism sibling. I limited 'Spirit gives life' to creation to avoid overlapping the regeneration sibling. I added objectives on the Spirit speaking through Old Testament prophets, providence, Bezalel's skill, general versus special revelation, New Testament citation formulas, organic inspiration in 2 Peter 1:20-21, and verbal plenary inspiration compared with rival views. All references are now verse-specific, and confessions are cited only where they state the doctrine taught.
